problem.value: Recent findings challenge the usefulness of Transformer models for time series forecasting because a simple linear model can outperform them.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, regardless of the complicated design of Transformer-based models, it is shown in the recent paper (Zeng et al., 2022) that a very simple linear model can outperform all of the previous models on a variety of common benchmarks and it challenges the usefulness of Transformer for time series forecasting.

contributions.value: Proposing the segmentation of time series into subseries-level patches as input tokens for Transformers.

evidence.quote: It is based on two key components: (i) segmentation of time series into subseries-level patches which are served as input tokens to Transformer; (ii) channel-independence where each channel contains a single univariate time series that shares the same embedding and Transformer weights across all the series.

contributions.value: Introducing channel-independence where each channel contains a single univariate time series sharing embedding and weights.

method_summary.value: The model utilizes a vanilla Transformer encoder as its core architecture under a channel-independence setting.

evidence.quote: Our PatchTST is illustrated in Figure 1 where the model makes use of the vanilla Transformer encoder as its core architecture.

method_summary.value: Input univariate time series are divided into patches to reduce the number of input tokens and computational complexity.

evidence.quote: Each input univariate time series x (i) is first divided into patches which can be either overlapped or non-overlapped.

method_summary.value: Patches are mapped to the Transformer latent space using a trainable linear projection and combined with a learnable additive position encoding.

evidence.quote: The patches are mapped to the Transformer latent space of dimension D via a trainable linear projection W p ∈ R D×P , and a learnable additive position encoding W pos ∈ R D×N is applied to monitor the temporal order of patches:

method_summary.value: Mean squared error (MSE) loss is employed to measure discrepancy and optimize the model.

evidence.quote: We choose to use the MSE loss to measure the discrepancy between the prediction and the ground truth.

method_summary.value: Instance normalization is applied before patching to mitigate distribution shift between training and testing data.

evidence.quote: It simply normalizes each time series instance x (i) with zero mean and unit standard deviation.

novelty.value: Patching univariate time series to reduce memory usage and computational complexity while allowing the model to process longer historical sequences.

evidence.quote: Thus constrained on the training time and GPU memory, patch design can allow the model to see the longer historical sequence, which can significantly improve the forecasting performance, as demonstrated in Table 1.

novelty.value: PatchTST naturally overcomes previous issues by masking patches rather than single time steps and removing the prediction head in favor of a D x P linear layer during self-supervised pre-training.

evidence.quote: Our proposed PatchTST can naturally overcome the aforementioned issues.

claims.value: PatchTST improves long-term forecasting accuracy significantly compared to state-of-the-art Transformer-based models.

evidence.quote: Our channel-independent patch time series Transformer (PatchTST) can improve the long-term forecasting accuracy significantly when compared with that of SOTA Transformer-based models.

claims.value: Training time is reduced by as much as 22 times on large datasets using patching.

evidence.quote: By setting patch length P = 16 and stride S = 8 with L = 336, the training time is significantly reduced as much as 22 time on large datasets.

claims.value: Increasing the look-back window L from 96 to 336 reduces MSE from 0.518 to 0.397.

evidence.quote: Table 1 shows that by increasing lookback window L from 96 to 336, MSE can be reduced from 0.518 to 0.397.

claims.value: MSE score is further reduced with patching when L equals 336.

evidence.quote: As evident in Table 1, MSE score is further reduced from 0.397 to 0.367 with patching when L = 336.
